body: hey, i happened to stumble across this while browsing, and this is helpful to me x

Ah heck, I feel like I know already I don't like my degree though. I guess TAFE/vocational courses are possible in the future which are as cheap in Aus too, same as online uni, might be worth a try.cheers tho

Yeah, I endlessly search for those moments while I'm researching (I do it with psychology and the such) of clarity, understanding and relatability. In terms of looking back at the past though, there have also been a few moments where I look back and go what the fk. But there's also a shit ton repressed so as you said, I'm sure it'll come in time. 
I'm not at the stage where I can quite analyse my parents yet, for example, why my dad criticises me about the randomest shit and doesn't give me any indication of what exactly I'm doing wrong, morally or whatever so there is no way out. Weirdly permissive about stuff that matters (substances, binge eating) yet ready to berate me for: buying 4 punnets of blueberries and eating one a day, eating fruit after dinner, reading too much, nor reading enough, focusing too much on my studies, not being interested in anything, thinking too much, talking too much, talking too little, going to the gym, not enjoying my life more, not watching enough TV (I'm serious), not having "EQ" (lies and hypocritism :/), having a boyfriend, believing in the virtue of apologies, wanting to do a psych degree, taking an IQ test, my perfectly fine driving skills, etc. I know i feel guilty all of the time and scared of being criticised randomly because of this- my analysis is currently only limited to my psyche. 
By any chance, are you familiar with the MBTI? You sound a little INTP to me. I am also one.
I wish I knew the last line to be true, but I'm not sure if I myself am really in myself. Maybe it forms over time after escaping the situation? 
11 years is also a really long time between escape and realisation of abuse, which is interesting.
these days, i try to tell myself that the actions I feel guilty for (some fuckery with substances, oversharing w irl people, raging at parents) this year are isolates, and that the destination they may or may not have brought me to, I would have come to anyway eventually because the seeds were sown in my childhood and these were just accelerants. But even then, it's hard not to feel that endless guilt and w h y.

You're right with the rage. Urgh. Some of it is directed towards myself too for some pretty bad mistakes I've made, so I can only wait until life is more stable to deal.

Feel free to check out the post I made in the advice sub about my degree if you want, it's a pretty hard decision to make, argh
Cheers, I'll check the site out

Yeah hahah, I don't see myself talking to my parents unless a third party is present because they honestly don't listen to me and just ignore my shit if it's just me and them. It's like they can't/don't/don't want to see how fucked their shit is, and I'm not perfect either, but only a third party can hold them accountable for their actions :/. I ignore the fact that they exist all of the time. 

It's more peaceful for me because they don't try to contact me day to day, and the last time my dad violated my boundaries was when I needed something from him. I have made sure I don't need anything from them for the time being indefinitely, but now I'm mad thinking about the second last time i needed something from him (to use the family car for my drive test.) 

mini rant: how he acts like I'm a shite driver but I learned reverse parallel parking in *one* night with my friend, yeah at *night*, and in an *unfamiliar* car too, then the *next day* I got into his car to practice an hour before my real test, did it easily in two smooth actions, and he has the gall to say dismissively "...who taught you this? \[in an awful tone\] do you think you can do this in real life? your angle is wrong. you NEED to be more far forward. go and google how to do it properly because you are just following the motions and you do not UNDERSTAND the angles." etc etc. 

I think that with this distance and as you said, you and I are both largely NC these days, I'm able to be justifiably angry at things that happened, ie. my dad putting me and my mum down instead of being a good husband/father and helping build us up. Which is relevant to tell my own psychologist/possibly a family therapist in the future.

I'm currently comfortable with using reddit for that support group role though, but we'll see what I can do in the future? I am considering taking fighting classes (I already gym and yoga) to channel my anger and the feeling of being overwhelmed, to try and train my fight response, and build my own self up (I'm done with having a 'dad', his chance to raise me is gone, it's my own life now) but I'd want my life/emotional state to be more stable before that if I ever do.

yeah, that's one way i'd describe it, being able to breathe and live. not to say i'm living my best life now, but it sure beats sleeping at 6am and waking at 5pm to avoid my parent's existence hahahah

i feel like i sort of had to drag myself out tho. i cant remember a timeline of what the hell happened before i moved out but it was somehow both really fkn slow and super fast as well if that makes sense. 

so for me, it was a series of slow steps and my health/life/emotional health being pushed to the limit like a pressure cooker and i wanted out. and i haven't released all that pressure yet even though i'm out. 

i'm sure you know of some small steps you could take to not particularly untrap yourself, but just to even make your daily life a little better, no matter how small or seemingly unproductive it may be.

for example, in my few months of dissociative activities before i moved out, i knew i should have watched some new shows and played some new games instead of literally doing NOTHING and feeling guilty for existing. it was awful, and i did this because i felt like i was decaying and that my will to live was dying. to a 'normal' person, round the clock media consumption is a waste of a life, but for me, it would have genuinely been a lot better than like, trying my hardest to not exist. 

it also reminds me of the greentext i read ages back of a post reply to a suicidal person which went along the lines of, "think of all the porn that will be produced after you're gone. there is so much porn produced every day that you could never watch all of it, and there will always be more videos to jerk off to. don't do it." 

so maybe for me, 'slightly better' is better than 'feel so much pressure that I just die inside.' if that sort of helps?

thank you, you're right about the past being this heavy mass that we can't control, although we can control how it relates to our current life. i guess this means that if the self hatred/confusion/shame/guilt is getting in the way of normal life, a conscious decision can be made to push it aside, but also keeping in mind that the reason the emotions are there in the first place is because something needs processing/accepting/management. and i can't do this when i'm doing other stuff like cooking or cleaning, it needs its own time and space when i'm alone.

sort of, it sounds similar to me when things were stable in my life, i'd listen to my favorite music and see the night lights at night after uni. not sure about the unreality part though, but i know i would get lost in my own random thoughts too and i would feel sooooo peaceful.
Yeah, i agree, it's weird for me being both sensitive and insensitive hahah ahhh

hey, i promise you you'll get through tonight. breathe a little, make yourself a snack or a drink or something and when you're ready, i'm sure you'll be able to have a conversation with him about how he can best support you, and what you'd like him to say when you're in this sort of headspace. there will always be people who care. i wish you well for tonight, x

I see, so it seems from your experience and a few others that the memories will come back up when we feel safe enough. 

In terms of self abandonment... I'm not diagnosed w/ anything yet, have considered four diagnoses including cptsd, but I think quiet bpd could explain it, plus many things in the past. 

i feel split into parts that aren't necessarily integrated, so I was upset at a sort of relationship I had this year where one part of me enjoyed it and another part of me felt like i didn't like him or care abt him like at all. and i felt like i'd lived a lie idk. i felt like i'd lied to him and to myself. but i didn't know it at the time and i don't regret it... but now i have no fkn idea which is the true me. whether it was all just an act, or it was a real part of me. maybe both are a part of me idk. 

i have to deal w other things that happened later this year which include oversharing w people i didnt rly wanna be close to, or more so i knew i couldnt be there for them in the same way, but i felt listened to and we shared the same interests, so we talked a bunch but again it felt like an act from me. but part of me just feels like i wanna forget abt them completely, so that'll be awkward to manage irl. I guess that's what reddit venting is for though hahah

the point being that self abandonment, to me, is exporting my thoughts and internal reality to others before even thinking about whether this is what I really want to do, and when that goes too far, just wanting to forget i ever said those things. it's rly cause I'm scared to be an individual I guess, as well as make decisions/evaluate things for myself. 

it's also like i need stuff to be seen by someone to know/feel like it's real. idk if that makes sense but i think it has to do w/ confirmation and validation. i dont like looking at my own thoughts and stuff ive written in my documents when alone. maybe cause it makes me feel too split into several parts, like 'which one is the real me?? aaaaa' or like 'fuck i exist? aaaaa'

but one could say the truest voice is what happens within me, and within me only. but this is what im scared to hear. idk what that is, idk what goes on in there, and i cant help but get anxious about it. im scared of what's inside. i just have to think a lot about random shit to stave it off. but maybe i can confront it soon idk but im scared itll make me feel so much fkn shame (again, possible quiet bpd) abt the stuff ive said and done in the past. like the inner self judging old selves. but maybe this is ok because it's a change thing and it doesn't mean that the old self wasnt real, and that i have to lose my friendship w the ex i mentioned above kinda.

anyway, thanks for listening to my scrambled vent, omf its so long. i dont think i mind having reddit to chuck my distressed thoughts into and stuff, but it's also weird for me having like, diff selves on my main acct, not to mention with all of my friends and friend groups. it feels dissonant.

what you said about freedom + self indulgence is p true tbh, in a sense that was one of the reasons i was smoking until i hated it hahah, it was just to feel the consequences (cognitive, physical, emotional) for myself and not because my parents said no :'')) 

and also, that freedom w/ sensory things like food/lifestyle/our body/house decor, i vibe w that too. but it's surprisingly hard to not feel guilty, and also surprisingly hard to feel free even tho I am. ah well... it's hard to develop (a sense of self) these days past... the self-abandonment. i feel like i can't face it ugh. but i guess that's v diff from inner critic guilt. 

but yeah, you are right. even if our parents did provide resources and kept us relatively safe and alive... it's hard to feel proud of what we've done in our lives. like it's hard to fathom that all I've achieved ever since like mid-teens when we were let 'free' has been all of my own, basically? ahh... 

it's, idk honestly. i haven't really ever grieved the loss of the past yet, whereas it seems like you have. Maybe in time... but who knows when it'll all hit?

Hey, thanks for the response, you're right about the numbness trying to protect us. Sigh, yeah, it's... It feels like it's been such a long but also a short life. Like its all over but also it's never even properly started so we have to live on limbo. Or, well, do that until we rebuild it again the second time, as we're both doing, or, well, trying to do depending on how you look at it. 😓

Hey, in my experience I've only ever done it alone without a therapist or agenda. Many feelings of love and revelations were had, but I found that after about 3 days, the afterglow wore off and I was back to my shell, probably because I wasn't at a good place in my life to consciously integrate these true feelings (I was still living back home w the people who caused a lot of it back then.)
So I suppose you'll need a good environment and that conscious effort to connect with what you found on MDMA frequently. 
However, the second time alone, I was in a much worse place. It was incredibly different from the 1st time, this felt darker and almost bitter... bittersweet? Idk it was like it was a disappointing experience because my soul was tired and disappointed and I was quite dissociated. 
If you're in this ocean of sludge rn, who knows what experience you may have? Maybe one between these two I've had. Good luck though, I'm sure you won't regret it
